component.name: Daylo
component.summary: See your whole year at a glance

description.p: Daylo is a habit tracker with a calendar you can read at a glance. Tick off what you did today and the year fills in with color, so you can see a streak forming or a month you let slip without reading a single number.
Everything stays on your device. There is no account to create, no server storing your days, and nothing sent anywhere. You can export a backup whenever you want and import it on another machine.

ul.li: Year view: twelve month heatmaps side by side
Month view: a dot per habit on each day, one tap to mark it
Current streak, longest streak and monthly completion
Export and import your data as JSON or CSV

screenshot.caption: The year at a glance, with activities and statistics
A month, with a dot per habit on each day

description.p: After about two weeks of use, Daylo asks once how it has been going, and opens an email if you want to answer. It also has an anonymous check-in. On a new installation it is on, and the app says so the first time it opens, with a link to look at it or turn it off; installations updating from an earlier version keep it off. Once a day at most it sends a random number made on your device, the app version, your system and the date, and nothing about what you track. The switch is in the menu, and turning it off sends one last note and deletes the number.

Daylo opens on the month, and the year is now one continuous calendar that can also be read a row per activity, or a block per week on a phone. The year can be walked with the arrow keys, saying the date and what you did on each day as you reach it. Android can remind you each evening at a time you choose. Streaks are counted one way everywhere: they no longer reset on the first of January, and they no longer read zero until the day is ticked. Tapping a button no longer leaves a ring around it.

Exporting now asks where to save the file and says where it went. Days in the year view no longer stretch when the pointer is over them, and the checkbox is drawn by Daylo rather than by the desktop theme. A backup is named after the local date rather than the one in UTC.
The app file is now called Daylo, backups are named daylo-backup, and a CSV export is no longer called a backup because only JSON can be imported back.
Stable download names, a permanent Android signing key, and the toggle log that keeps notes when a day is unmarked.
